items.title: Intismeran Autogene plus Pembrolizumab for Resected Stage IIB to IV Melanoma.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intismeran autogene (intismeran) is an individualized neoantigen therapy that is designed to induce new T-cell responses and expand preexisting T-cell responses against patient-specific tumor neoantigens, which may potentially improve the efficacy of adjuvant therapy in patients with melanoma.
METHODS: In this phase 3, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned patients with completely resected stage IIB to IV cutaneous melanoma in a 2:1 ratio to receive intramuscular intismeran (at a dose of 1 mg) or placebo every 3 weeks for nine doses; all the patients received intravenous pembrolizumab (at a dose of 400 mg) every 6 weeks for nine cycles. The primary end point was investigator-determined recurrence-free survival, assessed in a time-to-event analysis. Key secondary end points included investigator-determined distant-metastasis-free survival (assessed in a time-to-event analysis) and safety.
RESULTS: A total of 1137 patients underwent randomization: 757 to the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 380 to the placebo-pembrolizumab group. The median follow-up was 24.6 months. Recurrence-free survival at 24 months was 82.2% in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 70.0% in the placebo-pembrolizumab group (two-sided P<0.001); the piecewise hazard ratio was 0.99 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 1.49) before 6 months and 0.42 (95% CI, 0.30 to 0.58) after 6 months. Distant-metastasis-free survival at 24 months was 88.5% with intismeran-pembrolizumab and 80.2% with placebo-pembrolizumab (two-sided P = 0.002); the piecewise hazard ratio was 1.01 (95% CI, 0.58 to 1.79) before 6 months and 0.50 (95% CI, 0.34 to 0.73) after 6 months. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 23.6% of the patients in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 20.3% of the patients in the placebo-pembrolizumab group. Eight patients (1.1%) in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group died from an adverse event; five of the deaths occurred before intismeran was administered.
CONCLUSIONS: Adjuvant therapy with intismeran plus pembrolizumab significantly prolonged recurrence-free survival and distant-metastasis-free survival as compared with pembrolizumab alone in patients with completely resected, high-risk cutaneous melanoma. (Funded by Merck Sharp and Dohme and Moderna; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05933577.).

items.title: Safety, tolerability, and efficacy of bepranemab in people living with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tau aggregation is a defining feature of the pathophysiology of Alzheimer's disease and an appealing therapeutic target, yet tau-directed antibodies tested to date-primarily targeting N-terminal epitopes-have failed to slow tau progression or cognitive decline. Bepranemab targets the tau mid-region, predicted in cell-based assays to more effectively block neuron-to-neuron tau spread than anti-tau antibodies targeting the N-terminus. We aimed to investigate the safety and efficacy of bepranemab in slowing progression of tau pathology and clinical decline in people with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease.
METHODS: This double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial recruited participants across 101 outpatient sites in Europe (eight countries), Canada, and the USA. Participants (aged 50-80 years) with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease were randomly assigned 1:1:1 (using an interactive response system) to intravenous bepranemab 45 mg/kg, bepranemab 90 mg/kg, or placebo (every 4 weeks for 76 weeks), stratified by diagnosis, apolipoprotein E ɛ4 carrier status, and symptomatic treatment use. The primary endpoint was change from baseline to week 80 in Clinical Dementia Rating Scale-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) total score. Efficacy was assessed in the full analysis set (ie, all randomly assigned participants who received at least a partial dose of trial medication and had at least one valid post-baseline clinic visit and efficacy assessment). Safety was assessed in all randomly assigned participants who received at least a partial dose of the trial medication. No imputation was done for missing data. The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04867616) and is complete.
FINDINGS: Between Aug 24, 2021, and Oct 25, 2022, 466 participants were randomly assigned to bepranemab 45 mg/kg (n=154), bepranemab 90 mg/kg (n=155), or placebo (n=157) at 85 sites. Median age was 72·0 years (IQR 66·0-76·0), 259 (56%) were female, and 207 (44%) were male. In total, 460 participants were included in the full analysis set: bepranemab 45 mg/kg (n=152), bepranemab 90 mg/kg (n=152), and placebo (n=156). Least-squares mean CDR-SB total score change from baseline to week 80 was 2·15 in the bepranemab 90 mg/kg group and 1·85 in the bepranemab 45 mg/kg group versus 1·81 in the placebo group, with differences versus placebo of 0·34 (95% CI -0·09 to 0·78, p=0·12; 80% CI 0·06 to 0·63) for the bepranemab 90 mg/kg group and 0·04 (-0·40 to 0·47, p=0·87; -0·25 to 0·32) for the bepranemab 45 mg/kg group. Frequency of treatment-emergent adverse events with bepranemab was similar to the placebo group (139 [91%] with bepranemab 45 mg/kg, 140 [91%] with bepranemab 90 mg/kg, and 142 [90%] with placebo); no treatment-related neuroinflammatory safety signals were identified clinically or on brain MRI scans. There were adverse events leading to death in four (1%) participants in the combined bepranemab groups and six (4%) in the placebo group; none were considered related to the trial treatment.
INTERPRETATION: Treatment with bepranemab was associated with an acceptable safety profile. However, the primary endpoint was not met. Hypothesis-generating differences favouring bepranemab in tau PET and 14-item Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale should be tested prospectively in trials powered for tau PET outcomes and stratified by baseline tau burden and apolipoprotein E ɛ4 status.
FUNDING: UCB.

items.title: Loberamisal for Acute Ischemic Stroke: The LAIS Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Effective neuroprotective and neuroreparative therapies for acute ischemic stroke remain limited. Loberamisal is a small-molecule compound that dually targets the postsynaptic density 95 (PSD-95) pathway and α2 γ-aminobutyric acid type α (α2-GABAA) receptor.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of intravenous loberamisal for improving functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The Loberamisal for Acute Ischemic Stroke (LAIS) trial was a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 clinical trial conducted at 32 hospitals in China. Adults aged 18 to 80 years with acute ischemic stroke, a baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score of 7 to 20, and no prestroke disability (modified Rankin Scale score, ≤1) who presented within 48 hours of symptom onset were enrolled between July 24, 2024, and December 7, 2024, with final follow-up on April 8, 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive intravenous loberamisal (40 mg) or matching placebo once daily for 10 consecutive days, in addition to standard stroke care.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was achieving a full functional outcome at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0 to 1. Safety outcomes included adverse events, serious adverse events, and mortality.
RESULTS: Among 998 randomized participants, 997 received at least 1 dose of the study drug and were included in the primary analysis (502 in the loberamisal group and 495 in the placebo group). The median age was 64 years (IQR, 57-71), 336 participants (33.7%) were women, and the median baseline NIHSS score was 8 (IQR, 7-9). At 90 days, 350 participants (69.7%) in the loberamisal group achieved an mRS score of 0 to 1 compared with 279 (56.3%) in the placebo group (relative risk, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.12-1.36; risk difference, 13.28%; 95% CI, 7.24%-19.32%). Adverse events occurred in 441 participants (87.8%) in the loberamisal group and 439 (88.7%) in the placebo group. Serious adverse events occurred in 43 participants (8.6%) in the loberamisal group and 53 (10.7%) in the placebo group. All-cause mortality occurred in 6 participants (1.2%) in the loberamisal group and 10 (2.0%) in the placebo group.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among patients with acute ischemic stroke treated within 48 hours of symptom onset, intravenous loberamisal, compared with placebo, resulted in a higher proportion of patients achieving full functional outcomes at 90 days. Further studies are needed to validate these findings and establish whether the benefits could extend to a broader patient population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06517173.

items.title: First and Subsequent Major Cardiovascular Events With Oral Semaglutide in High-Risk Type 2 Diabetes: A Secondary Analysis of the SOUL Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In the Semaglutide Cardiovascular Outcomes Trial (SOUL), oral semaglutide reduced the risk of a first 3-point major adverse cardiovascular event (3-P MACE; including nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, and cardiovascular [CV] death). Total event analyses, assessing both first and subsequent events, can contribute to a better understanding of the impact of interventions on the total burden of disease; however, the effects of oral semaglutide on subsequent events are unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of oral semaglutide vs placebo on total 3-P MACE.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a prespecified secondary analysis of the double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven, phase 3b SOUL randomized clinical trial, conducted from June 2019 to September 2024 with a median (IQR) follow-up of 49.5 (44.0-54.9) months at 444 centers in 33 countries. Participants had type 2 diabetes and atherosclerotic CV disease and/or chronic kidney disease. Data were analyzed from December 2024 to August 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: Once-daily oral semaglutide (maximal dose 14 mg) or placebo, in addition standard of care.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Occurrence of total (first and subsequent) 3-P MACE.
RESULTS: Overall, 9650 participants (median [IQR] age, 66.0 [61.0-72.0] years; 6860 [71.1%] male) were randomized 1:1. In the oral semaglutide group, fewer first and subsequent 3-P MACE occurred (683 total; 579 first and 104 subsequent events) compared with placebo (791 total; 668 first and 123 subsequent events) (mean ratio, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.76-0.97; P = .01). For the end point of 3-P MACE plus non-CV death, there were 138 fewer total events with oral semaglutide (910 events) compared with placebo (1048 events) (mean ratio, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.79-0.95; P = .004). As previously reported, adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 749 (15.5%) and 559 (11.6%) participants receiving oral semaglutide and placebo, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Oral semaglutide reduced the risk of first plus subsequent 3-P MACE vs placebo, highlighting the benefit of oral semaglutide in reducing the total burden of clinical morbidity and mortality in this high-risk population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03914326.

items.title: Risovalisib for PIK3CA-mutated recurrent or persistent ovarian clear cell carcinoma: a single-arm, multicentre, phase 2 trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian clear cell carcinoma is a rare but aggressive and biologically distinct subtype of ovarian cancer, in which PIK3CA mutations are common. Advanced ovarian clear cell carcinoma is very difficult to treat, and after failure of platinum-based chemotherapy, therapeutic options are limited. We aimed to evaluate the anti-tumour activity and safety of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, for treatment of patients with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma.
METHODS: We conducted a single-arm, phase 2 trial of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, in 27 centres in China and 12 centres in Japan. Eligible participants were adult patients (aged 18 years or older, with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1) with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma and one to three lines of previous systemic anti-tumour treatment. Risovalisib was given orally at 40 mg daily in 21-day cycles until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or other protocol-defined reasons for discontinuation. The primary endpoint was objective response rate assessed by blinded independent review committee (BIRC) using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (version 1.1), among all treated patients with a confirmed PIK3CA hotspot mutation and baseline tumour assessments with measurable lesions per BIRC (efficacy analysis set). The primary endpoint was considered met if the lower 95% CI was greater than 8%. Safety analyses were performed in all patients who received at least one dose of risovalisib (safety analysis set). The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05043922) and is ongoing but no longer recruiting patients.
FINDINGS: Between Oct 6, 2021, and Jan 31, 2024, 93 patients were enrolled and received risovalisib. The median age was 49 years (IQR 43-58), all patients were female, 52 (56%) were from Japan, 41 (44%) were from China, and 63 (68%) had two or more previous lines of therapy. The median duration of follow-up was 14·5 months (IQR 8·6-18·3). The objective response rate was 29 (35% [95% CI 25-46]) of 84 patients in the efficacy analysis set. The most commonly reported grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events in 93 patients were rash (30 [32%]), hyperglycaemia (28 [30%]), and decreased weight (7 [8%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 36 (39%) patients, the most common being rash (eight [9%]), pneumonitis (six [6%]), and decreased appetite (four [4%]). There were no treatment-related deaths.
INTERPRETATION: These results support risovalisib as a potential novel treatment option for PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma, a rare yet lethal cancer in dire need of additional treatment options. Combination strategies including risovalisib could also be explored to further increase efficacy observed in this study.
FUNDING: Haihe Biopharma.

items.title: HOPO 14-1, an Oral Actinide Chelator: A Phase 1 Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Current treatments approved by the US Food and Drug Administration for internal actinide contamination (pentetate calcium trisodium and pentetate zinc trisodium) require intravenous injection or nebulized inhalation under medical supervision and have limited radionuclide coverage. HOPO 14-1, an oral form of 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO), is the first shelf-stable, broad-spectrum actinide chelator in clinical development that does not require intravenous access or trained personnel. In preclinical models, 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO) removed a broad range of actinides, and its oral route supports scalable emergency medical use.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic parameters, and excretion of a single dose of HOPO 14-1 in healthy adults.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a phase 1 nonrandomized clinical trial including 42 healthy adults (6 per dose level) with evaluations for 14 days after administration of a single dose and conducted at a single site in the US. Participants were recruited and screened between March 2023 and July 2025 and follow-up was completed in August 2025.
INTERVENTION: Single oral dose of HOPO 14-1 administered at 1 of 7 dose levels (100 mg, 200 mg, 500 mg, 1200 mg, 2500 mg, 5000 mg, or 7500 mg) with follow-up through day 14 after dose administration.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were the incidence and severity of adverse events, drug-related adverse events, and serious adverse events. The secondary outcomes were plasma pharmacokinetic parameters and cumulative urinary and fecal excretion.
RESULTS: Of the 42 healthy adults enrolled (median age, 43 [IQR, 34-51] years; 64% female), all received a single dose of HOPO 14-1 (administered across all dose levels as assigned). There were no serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxic effects. The drug-related adverse events included diarrhea (31%), vomiting (14%), headache (12%), and fatigue (7%); all were mild to moderate in severity. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the principal tolerability findings and most evident at the highest doses. The plasma pharmacokinetic parameters demonstrated rapid absorption (median time of maximum plasma concentration, 0.86 [range, 0.53-1.60] hours to 1.90 [range, 1.40-2.90] hours) and dose-dependent increases in systemic exposure, with greater than proportional increases at higher doses. Fecal excretion was the primary route of elimination; urinary excretion was minimal.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Single oral doses of HOPO 14-1 up to 7500 mg were administered without dose-limiting toxicity or serious adverse events in healthy adults. Gastrointestinal tolerability defined the practical single-dose ceiling. These findings establish the first human safety and pharmacokinetic profile of a novel, orally administered actinide chelator and support further clinical evaluation of HOPO 14-1 as a countermeasure for internal radionuclide and heavy metal contamination. Development of a deployable and population-level emergency intervention addresses a long-standing unmet need with important implications for public health preparedness.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05628961.

items.title: Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy for obesity: a randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: Incretin mimetics as obesity therapy induce substantial weight and fat loss but also decrease lean soft tissue mass, possibly impairing skeletal muscle function. Here, in this two-arm randomized controlled trial of adding resistance exercise (REx) to tirzepatide (T), 120 adults with overweight or obesity were treated with tirzepatide and randomized to thrice-weekly resistance exercise training or usual activities for 40 weeks. Tirzepatide was safe, and most participants tolerated up-titration to 15 mg weekly. Adherence to resistance exercise was 91%. Weight loss achieved was similar (T = -22.61 kg, T+REx = -22.28 kg, P = 0.694). For primary outcomes, loss of total fat mass was similar (T = -17.19 kg, T+REx = -17.98 kg, P = 0.700; between-group difference = -0.77 kg, 95% confidence interval (CI): -2.14 kg to 0.60 kg), but resistance exercise reduced loss of total lean soft tissue mass (T = -4.67 kg, T+REx = -3.57 kg, P < 0.001; between-group difference = 1.09 kg, 95% CI: 0.43-1.75 kg). For related endpoints, resistance exercise reduced loss of appendicular lean soft tissue mass (T = -3.55 kg, T+REx = -2.92 kg, P < 0.001). Upper and lower body muscle strength decreased with tirzepatide (bench press -4.09 kg, lat pulldown -4.42 kg, knee extension -4.42 kg) but increased with T+REx (+4.68 kg, +8.58 kg, +5.88 kg, respectively, all P < 0.001 versus tirzepatide). items.title: An ulcerative colitis taxonomy defined by individual patient-reported response trajectories.
items.abstract: A barrier to precision medicine for ulcerative colitis (UC) is the inability to predict and mechanistically explain treatment responses. Using patient-reported outcomes (PROs) from a phase 3b comparative trial of 768 participants, we identified four distinct patient response-trajectory groups for vedolizumab (anti-integrin) and adalimumab (antitumor necrosis factor). Validation in a second phase 3 trial of 576 participants linked PRO-defined vedolizumab trajectories to long-term disease complications. Bulk, single cell, and spatial transcriptomics and proteomics identified vascular inflammation as associated with vedolizumab nonresponse through interactions between SPP1+ macrophages and endothelial cells. In two separate real-world cohorts of 4,981 and 3,854 patients with UC, concomitant use of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (modulators of vascular inflammation) was associated with reduced long-term complications for vedolizumab but not anticytokine therapies. These findings define a response-trajectory-based taxonomy that requires prospective validation for clinical utility and applications for selecting vedolizumab combination therapy in UC.

items.title: Micro-axial flow pump vs veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for high-risk percutaneous coronary interventions: a randomized trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The efficacy of prophylactic mechanical circulatory support with micro-axial flow pump or veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) in patients with severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) undergoing high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.
METHODS: Patients with complex three-vessel disease, unprotected left main coronary disease or last patent conduit and LVEF ≤ 35% were assigned to receive either a micro-axial flow pump (SynFlow 3.0) or VA-ECMO support during a non-emergent high-risk PCI procedure in this prospective, multicentre, randomized, open-label, non-inferiority trial. The primary endpoint was the incidence of 30-day major adverse events, defined as any of: all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke/transient ischaemic attack, repeat revascularization, major bleeding, acute kidney injury, cardiopulmonary resuscitation/cardioversion, cardiac surgery/limb ischaemia, or serious device-related complications. Safety endpoints included adverse events and serious adverse events.
RESULTS: The primary endpoint, 30-day major adverse events, occurred in 8 of 109 patients (7.34%) in the SynFlow 3.0 group and 13 of 113 patients (11.5%) in the VA-ECMO group (absolute difference adjusted for centre effect, -4.6%; 95% confidence interval, -12.6% to 3.5%; P for non-inferiority < .001). Patients with SynFlow 3.0 had shorter post-procedural hospital stay (4.1 days vs 5.2 days on average, P = .047) and fewer device-related adverse events (3.7% vs 11.5%; P = .041). Anaemia occurred more often with VA-ECMO than with SynFlow 3.0 (20.4% vs 9.2%; P = .023).
CONCLUSIONS: The prophylactic use of a micro-axial flow pump during high-risk PCI procedures was non-inferior to VA-ECMO in the incidence of 30-day major adverse events. The use of a micro-axial flow pump was associated with shorter post-procedural hospital stay and fewer device-related adverse events.

items.title: Left bundle branch area vs biventricular pacing for cardiac resynchronization therapy: the LEFT-BUNDLE-CRT trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Conduction system pacing has emerged as an alternative to biventricular pacing (BiVP) for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). The left-bundle CRT trial evaluated whether left-bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is non-inferior to BiVP in patients eligible for CRT.
METHODS: The left-bundle CRT trial was a multi-centre, randomized, investigator-initiated, and non-inferiority study. Patients with guideline-based CRT indications and left-bundle branch block per Strauss criteria were randomized to BiVP-CRT or LBBAP-CRT. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with a positive CRT response at 6-months, defined as either an improved clinical composite score (CCS) or a ≥15% reduction in left ventricular end-systolic volume. The non-inferiority margin was the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval (CI) and was set at 10%. Patients were followed for 12-months; secondary endpoints included echocardiographic, clinical, and quality-of-life outcomes.
RESULTS: The baseline characteristics of the 176 patients randomized to BiVP-CRT (n=84) or LBBAP-CRT (n=92) were similar, except for a wider intrinsic QRS in the LBBAP group: median 172 ms [IQR 158-184] vs. 165 ms [152-180]; P=0.04. Crossovers occurred in 26 patients (14.9%). In the intention-to-treat analysis, the primary endpoint was achieved in 94.6% of BiVP-CRT and 89.7% of LBBAP-CRT patients (RR 0.95; 95% CI 0.88-1.02), not meeting non-inferiority. CCS improved in 77% and 68% of patients randomized to BiVP-CRT and LBBAP-CRT, respectively and 85% and 79% had a ≥15% reduction in left ventricular end-systolic volume. Rates of adverse events and heart failure hospitalization were similar between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In CRT candidates with typical LBBB, LBBAP-CRT was not shown to be non-inferior to BiVP-CRT. Both strategies yielded high response rates and similar clinical outcomes.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of oliceridine versus remifentanil for analgesia in mechanically ventilated critically ill adults (CO-ROAM): a multicenter, assessor-blinded, non-inferiority randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract:
PURPOSE: Remifentanil provides effective analgesia during invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), but its utility is limited by opioid-related adverse events. Oliceridine, a G protein-biased μ-opioid receptor agonist, may decouple analgesia from these effects, but lacks evidence in critically ill patients.
METHODS: This multicentre, assessor- and patient-blinded, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial was conducted across 19 intensive care units (ICUs) in China. Adults receiving IMV were randomised 1:1 to oliceridine or remifentanil, titrated to a Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool score below 3. The primary endpoint was time in target analgesic range (TTR; non-inferiority margin -10%).
RESULTS: Of 307 randomised patients, 304 comprised the modified intention-to-treat population (151 oliceridine, 153 remifentanil). Median TTR was 96.0% versus 92.3% (absolute difference 3.7%, 95% CI -0.3-5.7%). Oliceridine was associated with fewer mild-to-moderate adverse drug reactions (ADRs), occurring at 15.9 versus 22.2 events per 100 patient-days (IRR 0.72, 95% CI 0.52-1.00, P = 0.049), and a lower rate of respiratory depression during the study period (0% vs. 4.6%, P = 0.015). Post-extubation respiratory depression (0% vs. 7.9%, P = 0.005) and analgesic-sedation costs were both lower with oliceridine. IMV duration, ICU stay, and 28-day mortality did not differ. Subgroup analyses identified a nominal ADR benefit in patients with Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II > 17 and a larger nominal TTR difference in those without acute respiratory distress syndrome.
CONCLUSION: Oliceridine provides non-inferior analgesia to remifentanil with a more favourable respiratory safety profile and lower costs in critically ill adults.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06454292 (registered June 11, 2024).

items.title: A nurse-coordinated intervention programme vs standard of care after an acute coronary syndrome: the ALLEPRE trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: There is a lack of long-term outcome data supporting the role of nurses in cardiovascular (CV) risk management. The ALLEPRE [ALLiance for sEcondary PREvention after an acute coronary syndrome (ACS)] trial was a pragmatic, randomized, multicentre, interventional trial comparing the efficacy of a nurse-coordinated prevention program (NCPP) with standard of care (SOC).
METHODS: The NCPP patients attended nine individual educational sessions over four years at which a centrally trained nurse provided counselling aimed at identifying CV risk factors and encouraging healthier lifestyles and medication adherence; the SOC patients followed the standard practices of their hospitals. The trial's primary endpoint was the composite of CV death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and non-fatal stroke (MACE).
RESULTS: A total of 2057 ACS patients were randomized 1:1 to the NCCP (n=1031) or SOC group (n=1026). In comparison with SOC, the NCPP significantly reduced MACE [16.2% vs 22.6%; hazard ratio (HR) 0.70; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.57-0.85; P-value <0.001], a benefit mainly driven by a reduction in non-fatal MI (9.3% vs 15.2%; HR 0.60; 95% CI 0.46-0.77; P-value=0.0001). The occurrence of the pre-specified secondary outcome of MACE plus ischaemia-driven revascularization was significantly reduced (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.64-0.92; P-value= 0.005). Exercise frequency (P<0.0001), body weight control (P=0.003), and medication adherence (P<0.001) improved more in the NCPP group.
CONCLUSIONS: The NCPP significantly reduced long-term MACE, improved physical activity, body weight control, and pharmacotherapy adherence in post-hospitalization ACS patients. Including an NCPP in healthcare provision may contribute to the successful implementation of secondary prevention strategies.

items.title: Off-Pump versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Prefrail and Frail Patients: 30-Day and 1-Year Outcomes From the FRAGILE Randomized Trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain.
METHODS: This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated.
RESULTS: A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0-73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94-2.31]; P=0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P=0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively (P=0.099).
CONCLUSION: In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02338947.

items.title: Osimertinib, platinum, and etoposide for patients with metastatic EGFR/TP53/RB1-mutant lung cancers at risk for histological transformation.
items.abstract: Although EGFR inhibitors are highly effective for treating EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinomas (EGFR+ LUADs), resistance inevitably emerges, with histologic transformation to small cell lung cancer (SCLC) representing a particularly aggressive mechanism. Our prospective trial enrolled patients with EGFR+ LUAD at high risk of transformation (TP53/RB1-deficient) and treated them with first-line osimertinib combined with platinum and etoposide. Despite the addition of SCLC-directed chemotherapy, nearly half of patients (5 of 11) underwent SCLC transformation, with median progression-free survival of 11 months and overall survival of 33 months. Genomic and single-cell transcriptomic profiling of patient samples revealed clinical and subclinical plasticity associated with TP53/RB1 comutations, including histological transformation to SCLC, as well as mesenchymal and squamous histologies. These changes in plasticity were linked to progressive disruption of the RB pathway, leading to altered chromatin accessibility and induction of neuronal differentiation and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition transcriptional programs, further intensified by osimertinib treatment. These findings provide insights into the role of plasticity in mediating drug tolerance.
